goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` uses `String#scrub`, introduced in Ruby 2.1 (Dec 2013), which may postdate the Ruby version this 2013-era app actually targets, risking NoMethodError on every feed poll (confidence=55, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, and `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies (e.g., 1.9.x/2.0). However, the diff does not specify the project’s required Ruby version (no `.ruby-version`, no `ruby 'x.y.z'` in the Gemfile), so concluding this will “risk NoMethodError on every feed poll” depends on an external assumption about runtime Ruby. The only hint is a Gemfile comment about perftools and 1.9, which is not strong enough to make this a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused in the file and looks like a copy-paste leftover; if unresolvable it raises LoadError every time the job class loads, breaking the whole embed-retrieval path (confidence=50, severity=P1)

The diff does not show whether `email/sender` exists in the codebase, nor that this `require_dependency` would fail. As written, it’s an unused require/perf/cleanup nit unless the file is missing, which is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `import_remote` fetches via plain `open(url).read` with no timeout, redirect limit, or size cap, so a slow/huge/hanging remote host stalls a sidekiq worker or exhausts memory (confidence=85, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` after requiring `ruby-readability`. This uses `open-uri` to fetch arbitrary remote content with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, redirect limit, or response size cap. The method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (used by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) and from the Disqus import task, so a slow/hanging host or very large response can block a Sidekiq worker thread/process or consume excessive memory when `.read` slurps the whole body. This is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — feed fetch via `open(...)`+`SimpleRSS.parse` has no timeout/size limit and no rescue, so a slow/huge/malformed feed hangs or OOMs the hourly job (confidence=75, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no timeout options (e.g., open_timeout/read_timeout) and no rescue around network/parse errors. This can cause the scheduled hourly job to block on a slow/unresponsive feed URL, or raise and fail on malformed responses, and it also provides no protection against very large responses being read/parsed in memory. The diff introduces this behavior directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — existence check then `create!` is not transactional/locked; concurrent imports of the same URL can raise unrescued RecordNotUnique (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a read-then-create pattern: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a `Topic.transaction` and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent imports of the same `url` can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/unique constraint violation. There is no rescue/retry or locking around the existence check, so the exception can escape (e.g., from `Jobs::PollFeed` or `TopicRetriever`). The surrounding transaction does not prevent this race because it doesn’t lock the `topic_embeds` row (it doesn’t exist yet).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:52 / app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:16 — no rescue around `TopicEmbed.import_remote`; network errors, HTTP errors, and Readability parse failures are unhandled and untested (confidence=80, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document.new(...)` without any error handling. This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb) and thus from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job. `open-uri` can raise network/HTTP exceptions (timeouts, DNS, 404s, etc.) and Readability parsing can also raise; with no rescue, these will bubble up and fail the job/request path. The added specs only cover host/throttle behavior and do not test failure modes of `import_remote`, so the “unhandled and untested” claim matches the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130-133 — raw_html posts skip the entire cook/sanitize pipeline with no test asserting script/style/on* attributes are stripped from imported content (confidence=60, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` uses this path when creating posts from external content (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`). That imported content comes from RSS/HTTP (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`) and is not sanitized before being stored/rendered; the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The added spec (`topic_embed_spec`) even asserts `post.cooked.should == post.raw`, reinforcing that no sanitization occurs. This is a verifiable security/correctness issue in the diff (XSS risk from untrusted HTML).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:354 / lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 / app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `embeddable_host` is free text with no format validation/normalization; scheme, port, or case mismatches silently break embedding (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: `embeddable_host` is defined as a plain string setting with no validation/normalization (config/site_settings.yml). The runtime checks compare it directly to `URI(...).host` (EmbedController#ensure_embeddable: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; TopicRetriever#invalid_host?: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). Since `URI(...).host` returns only the hostname (no scheme/port) and may be normalized differently (e.g., lowercased), common admin inputs like `https://example.com`, `example.com:443`, or different casing/whitespace will not match and will cause embedding/retrieval to be rejected or silently skipped. This is a verifiable correctness/usability defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-143 — `--category` option and all category-assignment logic deleted with no replacement or warning; existing invocations silently lose that data (confidence=65, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the `category_id` lookup and the `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` usage. The new path (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`) does not accept or set a category, so the Disqus import task no longer supports importing into a specified category. This is a real behavior/API regression for existing users of the task, though it would typically fail with an unknown option rather than “silently” preserving the invocation while dropping the category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14-19 — no per-client rate limiting on `best`; only a 60s-per-URL redis throttle inside the job, so distinct URLs are unthrottled (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best` (lines 14-19 in the new file), when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for the provided `embed_url`. The only throttling added in this diff is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which uses a Redis key of `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` with a 60s TTL—i.e., it throttles per *URL*, not per client/IP/user/session. Therefore a client can submit many distinct `embed_url` values (still passing `ensure_embeddable` and host checks) and cause unthrottled job enqueueing / remote fetch attempts, which is a real rate-limit/DoS exposure introduced by the new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — `method_option :category`/`-c` deleted without replacement, a functional regression not called for by an "embed URL handling and validation" task (confidence=85, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `method_option :category` and the associated `category_id` lookup, so the Thor task no longer supports choosing a category. However, this is a deliberate, self-consistent change: the code no longer references `options[:category]` and now imports via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` instead of `PostCreator` with a `category` parameter. Whether this is an unintended regression or “not called for” cannot be verified from the diff alone (it’s a behavior/feature change, not a clear bug or defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — disqus.thor's post-creation path rewired from `PostCreator.new(...).create` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, an unrelated importer rewrite bundled into this task (confidence=75, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to create the initial topic via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` instead of `PostCreator.new(...).create`, and it also removes the `--category` option. However, the proposed finding frames this as an “unrelated importer rewrite bundled into this task,” which is primarily a scope/cohesion complaint rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff. From the diff alone, it’s plausible this is an intentional refactor to reuse the new embedding/import pipeline, not a clear problem by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:1 — an entirely new hourly RSS/Atom feed-polling job (new site settings + new gem) is content-ingestion scope, not "embed URL handling and validation" (confidence=80, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` (hourly) plus site settings and gems (`simple-rss`, `ruby-readability`) to ingest RSS/Atom content and import it as topics/posts. However, the proposed finding is essentially a scope/commentary concern (“content-ingestion scope, not embed URL handling and validation”), not a verifiable bug, security flaw, or correctness defect introduced by the code. Nothing in the diff indicates this is unintended or broken—it's a deliberate new feature that is gated behind `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` and related settings. Therefore it does not qualify as a REAL problem per the criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:63 — new `cook_methods` enum + `cook` bypass is content-pipeline/rendering scope, not URL handling or validation (confidence=65, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces `Post.cook_methods` and a `cook` fast-path that returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html` (used by `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The proposed finding merely characterizes this as “content-pipeline/rendering scope, not URL handling or validation,” which is not a verifiable defect (no incorrect behavior, security issue, or bug is identified). It reads as a scope/concern comment rather than a concrete problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save` changed to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, altering shared save behavior for all callers to support embed-import, broader than stated scope (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. This only alters behavior when a caller explicitly passes `skip_validations: true` (newly used by `TopicEmbed.import` when revising imported content). For all existing callers that do not set this option, behavior remains the same (validations still run). Since bypassing validations is explicitly requested via the option and is consistent with the embed-import use case in the diff, this is not a clear defect introduced by the change—it's an intentional, opt-in behavior change rather than an unscoped regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to a pre-existing, already-shipped, unrelated migration with no traceability to the embed task (confidence=65, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing migration (CreateTopTopics) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, but this does not introduce a verifiable defect in the application as shown. Rails migrations are applied based on their version; changing an already-applied migration file won’t affect existing installations, and for fresh installs the table won’t exist yet so `force: true` won’t drop data. The finding’s main complaint ("unrelated" / "no traceability") is a process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness issue evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fetches/buffers arbitrary remote content with no timeout/redirect limit/size cap, reachable by any anonymous visitor via `/embed/best` (confidence=80, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full buffered body into `Readability::Document.new(...)` with no explicit open/read timeouts, redirect limits, or response size cap. This can hang a worker thread or consume large memory if the remote endpoint is slow or returns an unexpectedly large payload. The fetch is reachable from `/embed/best` when no existing `TopicEmbed` exists: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Access is not authenticated (uses `current_user` which may be nil), and while `TopicRetriever` restricts `embed_url` host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (so it’s not fully “arbitrary remote content”), it is still an unbounded remote fetch triggered by anonymous requests with a suitable Referer/URL host match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` has no timeout/size bound and runs hourly via cron with no guard (confidence=70, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Ruby `open-uri` without any explicit `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, or response size limit, and it runs as a scheduled hourly Sidekiq job. This can cause the job/worker to hang or consume excessive memory if the remote feed is slow/unresponsive or very large. The finding’s “no guard” wording is slightly off because `execute` does guard on `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`, but those guards don’t address the lack of network timeouts/size bounds, so the core issue is real and visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — check-then-act against the `embed_url` unique index with no `rescue RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid`; two concurrent importers of the same URL raise an unhandled DB exception (confidence=75, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` (inside a transaction) while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With two concurrent importers for the same `url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the second will raise an unhandled DB uniqueness exception (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`). There is no `rescue`/retry or atomic `find_or_create_by` to handle this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33 vs app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-38 — redis throttle only guards TopicRetriever's entry point; PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import directly, bypassing it entirely (confidence=65, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is clearly intended to rate-limit *user-triggered* embed retrievals for a specific `@embed_url` (it keys on `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) before doing network work in `perform_retrieve`. `Jobs::PollFeed` is a separate scheduled job (`recurrence { hourly }`) that is designed to poll a configured feed and import/update items; it correctly relies on `TopicEmbed.import` to de-duplicate via the unique `embed_url` index and `content_sha1` change detection. While `PollFeed` does not use the same throttle, that is not a verifiable defect in this diff—it's expected behavior for a scheduled importer, and it doesn't “bypass” correctness/safety because `TopicEmbed.import` already guards against repeated creation and only updates on change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — `topic_id`/`post_id` have no FK constraint or index; a destroyed topic/post later causes `embed.post` to be nil and crash on revise (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` but only adds a unique index on `embed_url`; there are no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id` and no foreign-key constraints. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then immediately uses `PostRevisor.new(post)` without a nil check. If the referenced `Post` (or `Topic`) is deleted later, `embed.post` can become `nil`, causing an exception at runtime. This risk is enabled by the lack of FK constraints (and lack of cleanup hooks) in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130-137 — bare integer `cook_method` enum forks the canonical content pipeline into two tiers, silently skipping `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` for raw_html posts (confidence=70, severity=P1)

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-11 + lib/topic_retriever.rb:35-46 — no persisted failure state/circuit breaker; a permanently failing URL is retried indefinitely via 30s auto-reload with no error UI (confidence=65, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally enqueues :retrieve_topic and renders loading. The loading view then reloads the page every 30s (loading.html.erb lines 6-11), causing repeated requests that each enqueue another job until an embed is created. TopicRetriever has only a short Redis throttle (~60s) and no persisted “failed” state; if the URL permanently fails to fetch/import (e.g., unreachable/404/parse error), TopicEmbed never gets created, so the iframe stays in an endless loading+reload loop with no error UI and a steady stream of enqueued jobs (many of which will just no-op due to throttling). This is a real behavior introduced by the diff and is verifiable from the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 + app/models/post.rb:130-137 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — RSS content stored as raw_html with zero sanitization and rendered via `raw post.cooked`; a malicious/compromised feed publisher achieves stored, forum-wide XSS (confidence=75, severity=P0)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces an explicit “raw HTML” rendering path for imported content with no sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, feed item content is taken from `i.content` (only `CGI.unescapeHTML` + `.scrub`, which does not remove scripts/handlers) and passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` causes `cook` to return `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, guaranteeing the HTML is output unescaped. This is a stored XSS vector if the polled feed content includes malicious HTML/JS (e.g., `<script>`, `onerror=`, etc.).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53 — Readability extraction whitelists href/src but doesn't filter `javascript:` URL scheme, enabling click-triggered stored XSS via crafted links (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds `Readability::Document` allowing `` and `` tags with `href`/`src` attributes, then stores `doc.content` via `TopicEmbed.import` using `cook_method: :raw_html`, which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` without going through the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. In the embed view it is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Nowhere in `import_remote`, `import`, or `absolutize_urls` is there validation that `href`/`src` use safe URL schemes (e.g., rejecting `javascript:`). This makes it plausible to persist a `javascript:` link in stored HTML and execute it on click in the embedded iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-19 — host is validated once on the initial embed_url; open-uri follows redirects without re-checking destination, enabling SSRF via a redirect on the allowed host (confidence=55, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but later `fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri). open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, and the code never re-validates the final redirected URL’s host/IP. That means an attacker can supply an `embed_url` on the allowed host that 30x-redirects to an internal/metadata address, resulting in SSRF from the Discourse server despite the initial host check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `ensure_embeddable` gates access solely on the client-spoofable `Referer` header, providing no real access control over triggering fetch/import of attacker-chosen URLs (confidence=70, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes access by comparing `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then allows the request (and sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). The `Referer` header is client-controlled/spoofable for non-browser clients, so an attacker can call `/embed/best?embed_url=...` with a forged Referer matching the configured host and cause `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url)` to run. While `TopicRetriever` later restricts `embed_url` to the same host as `embeddable_host` (so it’s not fully arbitrary-host SSRF), the controller’s access control is still effectively based on a spoofable header and permits unauthenticated triggering of fetch/import work for attacker-chosen URLs on that host (potential spam/DoS/content injection depending on settings).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added in-place to an already-shipped migration; a re-run (redo/partial-deploy replay) now silently DROPs the populated table instead of failing loudly (confidence=75, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` causes `create_table` to drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. This means that if this already-shipped migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, partial deploys, or replaying migrations on an environment where the table exists), it can silently delete populated data instead of failing loudly due to an existing table. That is a real correctness/data-loss risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` on the new table means any re-run unconditionally drops and loses already-inserted embed rows instead of failing loudly (confidence=55, severity=P3)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table if it already exists before creating it. While migrations normally run only once, this option makes a rerun (or running against a DB where `topic_embeds` already exists for any reason) destructive and can silently delete existing `topic_embeds` rows instead of failing and surfacing the inconsistency. This behavior is directly implied by the `force: true` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` with no `disable_ddl_transaction!`/batching performs a full-table rewrite under an exclusive lock on pre-PG11-era Postgres, blocking reads/writes on `posts` (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default generally forces a table rewrite and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, blocking reads/writes on `posts`. The migration as shown does not split the change into safer steps (add nullable/no default, backfill, then set default + not null) or otherwise mitigate lock time; `disable_ddl_transaction!` does not prevent the exclusive lock for a rewrite, but the core risk described (full-table rewrite / blocking) is real for that pattern.
